note: Teleon competitive/runtime LANDSCAPE — repos that do SLICES of Teleon, cataloged as substrate ADAPTER candidates / inspiration / adjacent registries. GOVERNANCE: none of these IS the Teleon runtime; Teleon's own local reference runtime + the CapabilityTask standard stay the stable layer. Durable-workflow/execution backends are interchangeable candidates BEHIND ExecutionProviderPort (numeric provider graph + governed fallback) — adopting one as primary must NOT create a second durable ledger / second worker framework / second event bus. Discovery != trust; candidate != active; output != truth. No raw keys.
conclusion: No single open-source repo combines all of Teleon's thesis end-to-end. The market validates adjacent pieces (K8s agent runtimes, agent-as-a-service, durable workflow engines, spec-first agent OS, agent sandboxes, agent/MCP registries, eval/RL-env generators). Teleon is differentiated as the CONTROL PLANE ABOVE them.
teleon_differentiators: purpose-defined capability object (CapabilityTask/PurposeTask) that stays STABLE while implementation evolves
runtime-neutral execution policy across local/function/job/K8s/browser/worker backends, switchable by policy/telemetry/pricing
side-by-side CANDIDATE implementations (parallel-path) compared against a baseline
EVIDENCE-gated promotion (benchmark/eval result is evidence, never promotion authority by itself)
reversible rollback (predecessor kept as a lossless rollback target)
object-level LLM preferences (OIPS) + numeric provider graph with governed, non-silent fallback
Baltor-style truth boundary: Teleon runs capabilities; Baltor governs truth; runtime/agent/LLM output is never truth
positioning_law: Teleon is NOT another agent framework, NOT another workflow engine, NOT another Kubernetes agent runtime. Teleon is the capability CONTROL PLANE ABOVE them: purpose, contract, runtime selection, evidence, promotion, rollback, boundary approval. These repos are candidate execution/sandbox backends or inspiration — never the Teleon abstraction itself.

entries.name: McKinsey ARK (Agentic Runtime for Kubernetes)
entries.what_it_covers: declarative, provider-agnostic, K8s-native agentic runtime; agents as first-class CRDs+controllers; defines WHAT agents do, not HOW — closest single project to Teleon's provision-by-purpose idea
entries.what_it_lacks_vs_teleon: no runtime arbitrage across non-K8s backends; no scorecard-driven candidate promotion / rollback / boundary-approval as the primary object; not a Baltor-style truth boundary
entries.do_not_adopt_as_primary: study + possibly wrap as a K8s backend adapter; ARK is not the Teleon control plane

entries.name: kagent
entries.what_it_covers: OSS framework to run AI agents in Kubernetes for DevOps/platform ops; multi-agent workflows; cloud-native
entries.what_it_lacks_vs_teleon: narrower than runtime-neutral CapabilityTask across functions/jobs/browser/local/customer-private; no eval-gated promotion object
entries.do_not_adopt_as_primary: candidate K8s agent backend behind ExecutionProviderPort; not a second control plane

entries.name: AgentScope Runtime
entries.what_it_covers: production runtime for agent apps: secure tool sandboxing, Agent-as-a-Service APIs, scalable local/K8s/serverless deploy, observability, framework compatibility
entries.what_it_lacks_vs_teleon: run/serve agents, not declare-stable-capability + generate-candidates + compare-to-baseline + gate-promotion + rollback
entries.do_not_adopt_as_primary: candidate agent-serving/sandbox/observability adapter; not the capability object

entries.name: kubernetes-sigs/agent-sandbox
entries.what_it_covers: Sandbox CRD for isolated, stateful, singleton agent-runtime workloads; scale-to-zero + resume-where-left-off
entries.what_it_lacks_vs_teleon: sandbox substrate only — Teleon would CONSUME it as a SandboxProviderPort/execution backend

entries.name: Temporal
entries.what_it_covers: mature durable-execution platform; workflows auto-handle intermittent failures + retries
entries.what_it_lacks_vs_teleon: not agent/capability-specific; not eval-gated self-adaptive compute by itself
entries.do_not_adopt_as_primary: candidate durable-workflow backend behind ExecutionProviderPort; the Baltor SQLite FleetLedger stays the local truth — adopting Temporal must NOT create a second durable ledger

entries.name: DBOS (dbos-transact-py)
entries.what_it_covers: Postgres-backed durable workflows, queues, scheduling, recovery, background-task guarantees; durable queues without a separate broker
entries.what_it_lacks_vs_teleon: no capability contract, runtime selection graph, candidate-promotion policy, or cross-runtime abstraction
entries.do_not_adopt_as_primary: strong LOCAL/private durable backend candidate; aligns with our local-first durable-store direction but does NOT replace the Teleon abstraction or become a second ledger

entries.name: Dapr Agents / Dapr
entries.what_it_covers: durable workflows, state, messaging, observability for reliable agent execution at scale; portable distributed-app runtime
entries.what_it_lacks_vs_teleon: substrate, not the full object model (purpose/success-criteria/runtime-policy/evidence/promotion/boundary-approval)
entries.do_not_adopt_as_primary: candidate agent-workflow-durability adapter; not the control plane

entries.name: Hatchet
entries.what_it_covers: orchestrates background tasks, AI agents, durable workflows; queues, retries, monitoring, alerts, logging
entries.what_it_lacks_vs_teleon: execution backend, not a CapabilityTask standard/control plane

entries.name: Inngest
entries.what_it_covers: durable functions replacing queues/state/scheduling; reliable step functions; AI workflow visibility
entries.what_it_lacks_vs_teleon: durable workflow layer, not a purpose-native self-adaptive capability object
entries.do_not_adopt_as_primary: candidate event-driven workflow backend behind ExecutionProviderPort

entries.name: Trigger.dev
entries.what_it_covers: OSS platform for AI workflows: long-running tasks, retries, queues, observability, elastic scaling
entries.what_it_lacks_vs_teleon: workflow/job platform, not a purpose-defined self-adaptive capability plane

entries.name: Q00/ouroboros
entries.what_it_covers: agent OS for replayable, specification-first AI coding workflows; turns nondeterministic agent work into a replayable, observable, policy-bound execution contract
entries.what_it_lacks_vs_teleon: focused on AI coding workflows; not generic cross-runtime selection; no Baltor-style truth boundary
entries.do_not_adopt_as_primary: spec-first/contract-first design reference; verify repo identity + license before any use

entries.name: agentregistry
entries.what_it_covers: registry for finding/managing/running MCP servers, AI agents, skills
entries.what_it_lacks_vs_teleon: registry/governance of agent artifacts, not a runtime/eval/promotion control plane
entries.do_not_adopt_as_primary: adjacent to OpenMCPHub/OpenToolsHub; verify before cataloging as a hub source
